text_blocks.snippet: Ovarian cancer, a malignancy of the ovaries, has a complex history intertwined with evolving understanding of its origins, risk factors, and treatment approaches. While the exact cause remains elusive, research points to a combination of genetic predisposition, hormonal influences, and environmental factors. The most common type, high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC), is now believed to often originate in the fallopian tubes.

list.snippet: Ovarian cancer has been recognized as a disease for centuries, with descriptions of ovarian tumors found in medical literature dating back to the 1800s.
In 1809, surgeon Ephraim McDowell performed the first known successful removal of a large ovarian tumor, though the exact nature of the tumor (malignant or benign) was not always clear.
